chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
The man does not perform sajdah upon anything upon which the rest of his body is not.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Humran, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

My father (peace be upon him) used to pray upon the khumrah (a small piece of flax), placing it upon the carpet and performing sajdah upon it. So when there was no khumrah, pebbles were placed upon the carpet where he would perform sajdah.

key_terms.الْخُمْرَة: Khumrah (a small piece of flax or cloth used for prostration)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid objects for prostration in Shia Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the physical validity of sajdah by ensuring the forehead rests directly on the earth or its natural produce, a key criterion in Shia fiqh to maintain the connection with the creation. It illustrates the practical application of this rule through the Prophet’s and Imams’ use of a khumrah (flax cloth) or pebbles placed on a carpet, distinguishing between the object of prostration and the supporting surface. This highlights the scholarly emphasis on simplicity and the prohibition of excessive elevation that might detach the forehead from the earth.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, from Ali<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The man cannot perform Sajdah upon anything which the rest of his body is not upon’.[1256] (p.s. – According to a footnote, this Hadeeth is in dissimulation)

Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, from Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Myasws fatherasws used to pray upon the ‘Khumra’ (a small piece of flax to perform Sajdah upon), making it to be upon the carpet, and heasws would perform Sajdah upon it. So when there did not happen to be a ‘Khumra’ (a small piece of flax to perform Sajdah upon), heasws would make pebbles to be upon the carpet where heasws perform Sajdah’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his father from Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who have said, ‘
One must not perform Sajdah (prostration) on an item on which none of the parts of his body rests.’” (According to Arabic footnote this Hadith is because of Taqiyah)
